cls: Angiotensin II receptor blocker (AT1 antagonist, ARB)
quick: 600 mg orally once daily (range 400-800 mg/day, once daily or in two divided doses)
May be taken with or without food
Contraindicated - can cause fetal harm/death; stop when pregnancy detected
Not recommended; unknown if excreted in human milk
Use with caution; no specific reduction routinely required but monitor in significant impairment
Use with caution in hepatic impairment
Alcohol may add to blood-pressure lowering
Blood pressure, serum potassium, renal function (creatinine)
summary: Eprosartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that selectively antagonizes the AT1 receptor, blocking the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II to lower blood pressure. It is indicated for hypertension, alone or with other antihypertensives. Like all RAAS-acting agents it is contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal toxicity), can cause hyperkalemia and renal impairment (especially with bilateral renal artery stenosis or volume depletion), and should not be combined routinely with other RAAS blockers or with aliskiren in diabetics.
indications: Treatment of hypertension, alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

dosage.d: Initial 600 mg once daily; usual range 400-800 mg/day given once daily or in two divided doses
dosage.n: Antihypertensive effect largely present within 2-3 weeks; max 800 mg/day

dosage.d: Correct volume depletion first or start at the lower end

admin: Take by mouth once daily, with or without food, ideally at the same time each day
Correct intravascular volume depletion before starting to reduce risk of hypotension
Maximal blood pressure response is generally seen within 2 to 3 weeks of starting or changing the dose
Do not use in combination with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
moa: Eprosartan selectively and competitively blocks the binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor in vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland. This inhibits angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion, leading to vasodilation, reduced sodium and water retention, and lowered blood pressure, without inhibiting ACE or affecting bradykinin metabolism (so it is less likely to cause cough than ACE inhibitors).

absolute: Pregnancy (can cause injury and death to the developing fetus)
Known hypersensitivity to eprosartan or any component
Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes mellitus
relative: Bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis to a solitary kidney
Volume or salt depletion (risk of hypotension)
Hyperkalemia or use with potassium-sparing diuretics/supplements
Severe heart failure or renal impairment (renal function dependent on RAAS)
monitor: Renal function (serum creatinine, especially after initiation)

preg: Eprosartan is contraindicated in pregnancy. Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal and neonatal injury and death (oligohydramnios, renal failure, skull hypoplasia, hypotension), particularly in the second and third trimesters. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
lact: It is not known whether eprosartan is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects on the nursing infant, breastfeeding is not recommended; a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment. In patients whose renal function depends on RAAS activity (e.g., severe heart failure, renal artery stenosis), eprosartan may cause oliguria, progressive azotemia, or acute renal failure. Monitor renal function; no routine dose reduction is mandated.
hepatic: Use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment. Limited data are available; monitor blood pressure and tolerability.

major: Aliskiren in patients with diabetes (contraindicated; increased risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, renal impairment)
Other RAAS blockers (ACE inhibitors, other ARBs) - dual blockade increases hypotension, hyperkalemia, renal failure
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes - hyperkalemia
moderate: NSAILs/NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of renal deterioration, especially in elderly/volume-depleted
Lithium - increased serum lithium and toxicity
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food interaction
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum potassium and creatinine; monitor electrolytes and renal function

serious: Acute renal failure / worsening renal function
Fetal toxicity if used in pregnancy

monitoring: Serum potassium (especially with renal impairment or potassium-affecting drugs)
Renal function (creatinine, eGFR) after initiation and dose changes
Volume status in patients on diuretics
counsel: Take once a day, with or without food, at about the same time
Do not take if you are pregnant or planning pregnancy - tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless advised
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially when starting
Report swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing, at once
Tell your doctor if you have vomiting, diarrhea, or dehydration, which can lower blood pressure too much
pk: Blood-pressure lowering begins within hours; full effect over 2-3 weeks
Peak plasma concentration about 1-2 hours after fasting dose
Antihypertensive effect persists over 24 hours with once-daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: ARBs like eprosartan cause less cough and angioedema than ACE inhibitors because they do not affect bradykinin
Eliminated mainly unchanged by biliary/fecal route with minimal CYP metabolism, so few CYP-based drug interactions
Correct volume/salt depletion before starting to avoid first-dose hypotension
Avoid dual RAAS blockade and avoid aliskiren combination in diabetics due to renal and potassium risks
Absolute contraindication in pregnancy is a class effect of all RAAS-acting drugs
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Limited data are available on overdose. The most likely manifestations are hypotension and tachycardia; bradycardia could occur from parasympathetic stimulation. Treatment is supportive: place the patient supine, give intravenous fluids to expand volume, and provide symptomatic care. Eprosartan is not removed by hemodialysis.
